# Digest

An incremental digest.

```rux
pub interface Digest {
    func Update(self: &var Self, bytes: char8[..]);
    func Finish(self: &var Self, into: var char8[..]);
    func DigestLength(self: &Self) -> uint;
    func BlockLength(self: &Self) -> uint;
}
```

Take one by generic bound and mutable reference — `func Sum<D: Digest>(digest: &var D)` — so work applies to
the caller's state without copying it.

## Requirements

<h3 id="update"><code>Update</code></h3>

```rux
func Update(self: &var Self, bytes: char8[..])
```

Adds `bytes` to what is being hashed.
Any split of the same byte sequence across any number of calls gives the same digest. An empty slice is
legal and changes nothing.

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to absorb |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Digest.rux#L31)

<h3 id="finish"><code>Finish</code></h3>

```rux
func Finish(self: &var Self, into: var char8[..])
```

Writes the digest into `into` and leaves the state unusable for further updates.
`into` must be at least [`DigestLength`](/docs/api/crypto/digest#digest-length) bytes; anything beyond that is untouched. Finishing twice is a
caller error rather than a supported operation — a digest is a one-shot summary of everything fed to it,
and an implementation is free to consume its state producing one.

| Name   | Type            | Description         |
| ------ | --------------- | ------------------- |
| `into` | `var char8[..]` | receives the output |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Digest.rux#L39)

<h3 id="digest-length"><code>DigestLength</code></h3>

```rux
func DigestLength(self: &Self) -> uint
```

How many bytes [`Finish`](/docs/api/crypto/digest#finish) writes.

**Returns**: how many bytes a digest occupies

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Digest.rux#L44)

<h3 id="block-length"><code>BlockLength</code></h3>

```rux
func BlockLength(self: &Self) -> uint
```

How many bytes the algorithm processes at a time.
Needed by the constructions built on digests — HMAC pads its key to exactly this — and by callers
choosing a buffer size that avoids splitting work.

**Returns**: how many bytes the compression function consumes at a time

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Digest.rux#L51)
